page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server featuring an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 3840 GB local NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate a balanced profile with notable strengths and specific bottlenecks. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show strong results, processing at 36.27 GB/sec and 14.14 GB/sec respectively. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier at 3390.33. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak, measuring 36.93 GB/sec for read-only and 19.38 GB/sec for write operations. CPU performance is average, with a Passmark CPU score of 23271.22 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 20287.03.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density by combining a dedicated 8-core Xeon processor with a substantial 128 GB memory array and a large 3.8 TB NVMe SSD. This makes it a highly capable option for workloads that require dedicated hardware without virtualization overhead. The server is well-suited for database hosting, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and lightweight LLM text generation tasks.
